response: A parent of three kids in the public schools is publicly apologizing to the educators and staff at South Portland School District, calling it beyond maddening that they're facing another large budget shortfall forcing the loss of more than 70 positions. As a taxpayer they feel the sting of it, but this is the predictable result of long-standing structural inequalities that starve public education while shielding the wealthy from contributing their fair share. These repeated cuts don't just disrupt schools—they disproportionately harm working families, communities of color, and the most vulnerable students who depend on adequately funded classrooms and protected educator jobs. It's time we demand real institutional reform to prioritize labor rights and equitable funding instead of letting these crises keep repeating.
